And when they were close to gaining a total victory, these Tatars,
an ambush of the Taghlibite Arabs of Shadwayh fell upon them from the left wing.
And the Tatars thought
that the enemy force had surrounded them from before and behind;
and those in the center of the battle-line turned their backs to flee along with the left wing.
Those, however, who were on the right wing—
who were by race Tatars called Oirats, along with five thousand Iberians (Georgians), and the king of the Armenians with his soldiers—
since they did not perceive the ambush of the Arabs,
broke with great force the Egyptians who were standing against them.
And they pursued after them as far as the gate of Homs,
and inflicted great slaughter among them,
until they heard of the flight of their companions;
and immediately they too turned back.
And on their return they encountered the Egyptian force that had returned from pursuing those Tatars who had fled.
And both sides shrank from one another,
and they fought and were killed,
and they broke through each other's ranks,
and each side crossed over to its own territory.
And thus the right wing of the Tatars arrived carrying great booty,
such as Egyptian pack-animals, mules, and gear.
While the left wing and the center even cast away their baggage,
and many arrived on foot,
buffeted by hunger and thirst.
And thus the right wing and the center of the Egyptians returned to Damascus with much booty that they had rescued from the Tatars.
And from the left wing of the Egyptians, only a few escaped,
being badly wounded and plundered.
And if Abagha had not come as far as the banks of the Euphrates and then returned to Baghdad,
the Egyptians would have been completely destroyed.
And in the winter of this year, there was a great burden upon the inhabitants of Assyria and the entire land of Sinjar, due to the return of these armies.
For there was also severe cold,
and much snow fell in this land of Mosul,
far more than was customary.
And after such a dissolution had occurred to both sides, the Mongols and the Egyptians,
certain marauders from the Ma'addites (Bedouins), Turcomans, and Kurds joined together,
and entered the territory of Cilicia.
